# Experiment 4: AI 3D Generation (TRELLIS, image-to-3D)

**Status:** Complete and verified. The asset was generated by a real AI 3D system, then imported, inspected, repaired, rendered and measured in Blender.
**Date:** 2026-10-24.
**Cost:** none. The Hugging Face Spaces were used anonymously on the free shared GPU (ZeroGPU), with no account, token or payment.
**Route chosen by the user:** free public web demo (image-to-3D).

![reference vs AI](renders/reference_vs_ai.png)
![repaired contact sheet](renders/generated/ai_generated_contact_sheet.png)

## 1. Generation system and record

| Item | Value (from [generation_settings.json](generation_settings.json)) |
|---|---|
| Generator | **TRELLIS** (Microsoft, open image-to-3D model) via the public Hugging Face Space `trellis-community/TRELLIS` |
| Access | The Space's Gradio queue API over HTTPS from [generate_trellis.py](generate_trellis.py) (standard-library Python). The in-app browser could not attach a local file to the Space's cross-origin app frame. |
| Mode | Image-to-3D, single image. **No text prompt.** TRELLIS-image takes images only. |
| Input | [reference/ref_three_quarter.png](reference/ref_three_quarter.png), 1024², transparent background. The Space removed the background and cropped. |
| Settings | seed 1234; sparse-structure guidance 7.5 / 12 steps; SLAT guidance 3.0 / 12 steps; mesh simplify 0.95; texture 1024 |
| Time | **26.9 s** end to end (21.2 s generation and GLB extraction on the server) |
| Output | `original_asset/single_view/trellis_output_2_sample.glb` (1,526,152 B; glTF 2.0 binary) and a 373 KB MP4 turntable preview. The original files are kept unmodified. |

**Failed attempts (recorded in [generation_logs/](generation_logs/)):**
1. **Hunyuan3D-2.1 (Tencent)**, `/generation_all`, shape plus texture. Refused: the endpoint requests 270 s of GPU time, which is above the anonymous per-task cap. The Space suggested a paid Hugging Face PRO subscription; that was **not** purchased. The first call also failed silently (`error: null`); the queue protocol revealed the real error.
2. **TRELLIS multi-image** (three-quarter, front, left and back references, matching the brief's "consistent views" workflow). Refused: the anonymous daily ZeroGPU quota was used up by the first run ("Try again in 23:57"). A Hugging Face token would raise the quota; none was used.

### Reference preparation (Phase 1)
- No concept artist was available, and the image-generation connectors (Figma Weave, Canva) need accounts and credits.
- The references were therefore **rendered from the Experiment 3 sculpt** with the shared palette ([make_reference.py](make_reference.py); [sheet](reference/reference_sheet.png)): three-quarter (primary input), front, left and back, all 1024² on transparent backgrounds.
- **Consequence:** this experiment measures how well an AI **reconstructs a given design** from one image. It does not test whether it can design the character from scratch.

## 2. Import and inspection of the original AI output (Phase 3)

[import_and_repair.py](import_and_repair.py) imports the GLB and applies **only** a uniform scale (×2.880) and a translation. That scales the snout-to-tail length to 2.885 m (the length of the other experiments), puts the feet on Z = 0 and the snout at y = −1.164. No rotation was needed: TRELLIS output already faces −Y.

The result is saved as [dragon_ai_original.blend](dragon_ai_original.blend) and rendered in the standard views ([sheet](renders/original/ai_original_contact_sheet.png)).

| Check | Original AI output | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Missing geometry | **None.** Four legs with claws, two wings with fingers, membranes and thumb claws, horns, spikes, tail, open jaw | The unseen right side and far wing were inferred plausibly |
| Distorted shapes | Wingspan 2.89 m vs about 2.65 m in other experiments, so it exceeds the reference box (X ±1.40) by 4 cm per side. The jaw is open (the reference's mouth line was read as an open mouth). The spike crest became ragged flat frills. | Proportions are close to the input elsewhere |
| Mesh continuity | **211 "shells", 3,565 open boundary edges, 220 boundary loops** | Almost all are **UV-seam vertex splits** from the GLB export. They disappear after welding (§3). |
| Surface normals | Inconsistent across the split pieces (1,898 faces flip when recalculated on the unwelded mesh); consistent after welding | |
| Polygon density | **8,337 triangles**, 6,149 vertices; isotropic triangulation from 95 % simplification | Very light. The wing edges and head silhouette are visibly polygonal. |
| Shading | **100 % flat-shaded faces**: faceted look in clay views | |
| UVs | One UV map, auto-unwrapped | Usable for texturing |
| Material | One material, one **1024² base-colour texture**. The BSDF is declared **Metallic 1.0, Roughness 1.0**, no metal/roughness map. | A fully metallic dragon; the albedo has some lighting baked in |
| Colour fidelity | Skin lighter and less saturated than the palette (value 0.36 vs 0.30, saturation 0.30 vs 0.43). **Horns and spikes drifted from bronze to salmon-pink/red.** The belly is yellower. **Eyes are a painted brown dot: no amber eye, no pupil, no socket.** | |
| Silhouette | **Strong.** It reads instantly as a winged dragon in all views (side silhouette) | |
| Buried surface (estimate) | 30.8 % of faces | An artefact of the unwelded open pieces (ray parity is unreliable on open shells); 0 % after welding |

## 3. Repair (Phase 4)

These repairs keep the design: geometry shape, UVs and texture layout are untouched.

| Repair | Result |
|---|---|
| Weld vertices within 0.5 mm (UV-seam splits) | −1,994 vertices. **211 → 2 shells**, 3,565 → **2** boundary edges (one 2-edge gap), 9 non-manifold edges |
| Remove tiny floating fragments (< 5 cm²) | None existed once welded |
| Fill small holes (≤ 16 edges) | Nothing fillable (the remaining gap is 2 edges) |
| Recalculate normals | 0 inconsistent faces |
| Shading | Smooth shading with sharp edges above 50° (claws and spike tips stay crisp) |
| Material | Kept the AI albedo; **metallic 1.0 → 0.0, roughness 1.0 → 0.55** (the palette skin roughness) |
| Texture colour alignment to the palette (HSV, region medians, AI paint variation preserved) | Horns and spikes (3.3 % of texels) → palette bronze; skin (77.2 %) → palette dark forest green; belly (8.3 %) → palette hue and saturation, brightness gain capped at 1.15 |

Two repair iterations were driven by renders:
- Setting metallic to 0 exposed the too-light albedo, which led to the skin alignment.
- The first, uncapped belly alignment (×1.53 brightness) produced clipped neon yellow with a hard edge, which led to the 1.15 cap.

Output: [dragon_ai_generated.blend](dragon_ai_generated.blend) and standard renders in [renders/generated/](renders/generated/). Repair is fully scripted; the whole import, inspect and repair script takes 3.2 s including Blender start-up.

**Not repaired (would require remodelling):** eyes (no socket or eyeball), open-jaw pose, ragged spike frills, polygonal wing trailing edges, wingspan proportion, triangle topology.

## 5. Evaluation

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Original geometry quality** | Surprisingly complete and coherent for 27 seconds: every anatomical item in the spec is present and connected, in one effectively watertight surface. It is **low resolution** (8 k triangles, faceted), the face is generic (no eye structure), the spikes turned into frills, and fine forms from the reference are softened. These include muscle masses, the brow, scutes and claw shapes. |
| **Repair effort** | **Low for integrity** (weld, normals, shading: fully automatic). **Medium for materials** (wrong metallic flag, colour drift; automatable by region-median alignment). **High for design defects** (eyes, jaw, spikes, proportions): these need remodelling or regeneration, not repair. |
| **Silhouette** | Very good and on-model; it inherits the reference's design |
| **Volume and form** | Good overall masses with soft, slightly lumpy transitions. Less defined than Experiments 2 and 3 because of the low polygon count. |
| **Materials** | The AI paints convincing colour zones (belly, horn and claw colours) on its own UVs, but with palette drift, baked lighting, low texel density and a broken PBR flag |
| **Real-time suitability** | **Best triangle budget of all experiments so far** (8.3 k triangles including texture and UVs). Triangle soup without edge loops, so not rig-friendly without retopology. Texture resolution is low for close-ups. |
| **Practicality** | Fast and free here, but **fragile access**: one of two endpoints refused the job (GPU cap), and the daily quota ran out after one generation. Reproducing or iterating needs an account or token, or local GPU hardware. Run-to-run variability (seed-dependent) was not measured because of the quota. |

**Key caveat for the final comparison.** The AI was given an image of our Experiment 3 model. Its good silhouette and anatomy are inherited, so they don't show that it can design. What it does show is that it can **lift a 2D concept into a light, textured, game-sized 3D asset in under 30 seconds**. That is a different and complementary capability from Experiments 1–3.

## 6. Lessons for an AI modeling skill
1. **Treat AI generation as a first-pass asset source,** gated by automatic checks: weld and seam count, shell count, normals, metallic/roughness sanity, a palette ΔHSV per region, and reference-box fit.
2. **Many "defects" are export artefacts.** The 211 shells and 3,565 open edges were UV-seam splits. Always weld before judging.
3. **Material flags from AI pipelines can be wrong** (a fully metallic surface). Validate PBR parameters, not just the texture.
4. **Colour drift is systematic and fixable** with region-median HSV alignment, but brightness gains need caps.
5. **Service access is the main risk:** GPU caps, quotas and silent errors. A skill needs fallbacks across several generators and a user decision on paid tiers or tokens.
